Halton Falls Trail completely exceeded my expectations. The trail is beautifully maintained, with stunning views throughout the ride. What really stood out was how, even with plenty of hikers and bikers around, there are long stretches of peaceful, quiet forest where you can truly soak in the calmness of nature. Everyone on the trail was incredibly friendly, which made the whole experience even better. This was my first 12 km MTB ride, and I absolutely loved every bit of it. There are also sections designed for more advanced riders, which makes it exciting to come back and challenge myself again.
Can’t wait to ride it again!

The waterfall is only a little trickle these days. We went on Tuesday afternoon, and it said that the park was "not busy". Making a reservation was really easy.

In terms of social distancing, the area by the waterfall was VERY busy. Most people were not keeping their distance from one another at all. I was a little overwhelmed by the sheer amount of people and their kids who weren't attempting to keep their distance from anyone else.

I found the rest of the park to be much more interesting and we hardly saw anyone else on the other trails. The views by the reservoir are really pretty! 

Pack your bug spray for this one (I feel like most trails are pretty buggy this time of year) and explore the conservation area beyond the waterfall for a really enjoyable hike! I recommend the Red Oak Trail!

If you enter the park via the main entrance, you have to pay for parking in advance, so be sure to park in the community entrance which is free - but head there early because it gets busy!! Be sure to bring your bug suit or spray, and visit the falls first to avoid the crowds!

Started our hike today at 9.30am. We walked in a clockwise direction and passed the waterfall early on. The first section of this trails starts out flat and wide then soon becomes very rocky terrain until you pass the waterfall. After this the trail became incredibly buggy and we wished we brought our big spray! There was a nice picnic bench when the bugs subsided for us to have a quick snack. The latter part of this hike was pleasant - wide trails and flat. We reached the stream/waterfall over the reservoir and contemplated taking the side trail back which runs down the right of the reservoir but stuck to the planned trail but looking back I wished we made this change. It wasn't too busy for a Tuesday morning either. We will come back, but big spray is a must!
